Modified assessment incorporating SLOOS:

- Policy and macro backdrop: Holding the federal funds rate at 1.50–1.75% remains mildly accommodative amid sub-2% inflation and strong labor markets. Implementation tools (IOER at 1.60%, T-bill purchases, term/overnight repo) continue to support smooth transmission.

- SLOOS overlay on credit supply/demand: Banks reported tighter standards and terms for C&I loans and for construction and land development lending, including higher credit score thresholds and tighter credit limits. Demand weakened notably for construction and land development loans, while consumer loan demand was generally unchanged to mixed across categories. Looking ahead to 2020, banks expect tighter standards for riskier loans (including C&I and CRE), reduced risk tolerance, and potential deterioration in loan performance and collateral values (including HELOCs), with only some portfolios expected to remain unchanged.

- Implications: Tightening credit supply and softer demand in business and CRE lending are likely to modestly restrain credit growth and business investment, partially offsetting the support from an accommodative policy stance. Combined with still-muted inflation, this tempers the otherwise slightly positive macro assessment.

Net: Slight positive, downgraded by tighter lending conditions signaled in SLOOS.
